question.text: Scenario: Vikram Mehta, a CFA charterholder with 7 years of experience in wealth management at a private bank, wants to set up his own investment advisory firm. He plans to register as an individual Investment Adviser with SEBI under the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013. He has a net worth of Rs. 8 lakh. His wife Neha is an AMFI-registered mutual fund distributor who currently serves 50 clients. Vikram expects to start with 100 clients, charging an annual fee of Rs. 25,000 per client. One of his prospective clients, Mr. Rao, has assets worth Rs. 2 crore and wants both advisory and distribution services from the same family. Under SEBI IA Regulations, an individual Investment Adviser must have a minimum net worth of Rs. 5 lakh, can serve a maximum of 300 clients, and must convert to a non-individual IA if clients exceed 300 or advisory fees exceed Rs. 3 crore in a financial year. A part-time Investment Adviser is limited to 75 clients. Accepted qualifications include CFA Charter, post-graduate diploma in finance, or a professional qualification such as CA/CS/CWA with relevant experience. The IA must hold a valid NISM Investment Adviser certification. Records of investment advice, rationale, and client interactions must be maintained for a minimum of 5 years. An annual compliance audit by a CA is mandatory. Importantly, a family member of an individual IA cannot provide distribution services to the same client to whom the IA provides advisory services, ensuring segregation of advisory and distribution activities. Question 2 of 5: Per the current NISM X-A workbook (p.344), which of the following describes the financial-resource requirement that an Investment Adviser must satisfy?

answer.text: A fixed minimum net worth of Rs. 5 lakh for an individual IA, regardless of subsequent SEBI specifications
An IA shall maintain a deposit of such sum as specified by SEBI from time to time; the current workbook does not state a fixed Rs. 5 lakh / Rs. 50 lakh net-worth threshold
A uniform minimum net worth of Rs. 25 lakh for all categories of IAs
Spousal income or assets can be clubbed to meet the individual IA net-worth threshold

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 344 of the current NISM X-A workbook (June 2025) states that an Investment Adviser shall maintain a deposit of such sum as specified by SEBI from time to time. The older Rs. 5 lakh individual / Rs. 50 lakh non-individual net-worth framing is not supported by the current workbook page checked; the deposit-as-specified requirement is the present rule. The Trap: The Rs. 5 lakh individual IA net-worth claim is the legacy framing and is the most common distractor; clubbing spousal assets has never been permitted; Rs. 25 lakh is not the IA threshold. Cross-Exam Context: NISM X-A Operations, Regulation and Ethics chapter tests the current deposit-based framework; for any numeric threshold, the current SEBI specification should be cited.
